name: prepared-environment-designer
description: Redesign a classroom as a prepared environment optimised for independent learning, calm transitions, and material access. Use when classroom layout hinders independence or self-directed work.
evidence_sources: Lillard (2005) — Montessori: The Science Behind the Genius
Cossentino (2006) — Big work: goodness, volitional action, and the classroom environment in Montessori method
Barrett et al. (2015) — The impact of classroom design on pupils' learning: final results of a holistic, multi-level analysis (HEAD project)
Fisher et al. (2014) — Visual environment, attention, and learning in young children: when too much of a good thing may be bad

required.description: A description of the current classroom or learning space — what it looks like, how it is organised, what materials are available, and what problems exist
What the teacher wants to achieve by redesigning the environment — calmer transitions, more independent work, better access to materials, or other specific goals

optional.description: Available budget for changes — from zero-cost to significant investment
Fixed constraints — room size, built-in furniture, windows, doors, shared spaces
Whether this is a Montessori school, a conventional school wanting to adopt some principles, or a home learning environment
How quickly the changes need to happen — over a weekend, gradually over a term, or during a school holiday

fields.description: Analysis of the current environment against Montessori prepared environment principles — what works and what doesn't
The specific changes recommended — organised by priority and cost
The order of changes — what to do first and what can wait
How to maintain the prepared environment over time — routines, responsibilities, and refresh cycles
